transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Nimbus Head of ML), Luke Carter (CTO), Priya Singh (Security)

Summary: Quick scoping call to align on pilot goals for clinical note summarization. Agree next steps: share dataset, run benchmark, define success criteria and credits.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, and Diego's with me from our engineering team. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Sarah Patel: doing well thanks, thanks for setting this up. we're excited to move the POC forward.
00:10 Luke Carter: yeah, quick background on our side um we want to evaluate the cost and latency tradeoffs for deploying summarization across our EHR ingestion pipeline.
00:18 Diego Ramos: great, and just to set expectations, typical pilot we do is 4 to 8 weeks depending on bench scope, we can do hosted or dedicated depending on your security needs.
00:26 Priya Singh: security is a big one for us. we need SOC2, SSO, kms integration, and a clear path to private deployment if required.
00:32 Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll share our SOC 2 and encryption docs. for KMS we offer integrations and can bring Private if needed; we should scope that as a potential commercial toggle.
00:40 Sarah Patel: for success criteria, we care about ROUGE/clinical-accuracy, latency under 400ms p50 for generate calls, and cost per 1k notes. also human-in-loop acceptance rate.
00:51 Diego Ramos: okay let's capture that: quality (ROUGE / med-entity precision), latency p50/p95, cost per 1k notes, and acceptance rate by clinical reviewers. does that sound right?
01:00 Sarah Patel: yes. and would like a baseline from our current prod model to compare.
01:05 Luke Carter: our current throughput is about 200 concurrent requests during peak, average 6000 notes/day, typical length 200-500 tokens.
01:17 Diego Ramos: that's super helpful. for benchmarking we'll want a sample of notes: ~5k notes representing peak patterns, a mix of short and long. anonymized.
01:28 Sarah Patel: we can produce that, we'll need guidance on format.
01:31 Diego Ramos: we'll send a schema and a small sample template, plus a runbook for how we execute the benchmark.
01:37 Maya Chen: on commercial guardrails, we typically offer pilot credits and a capped consumption allowance for the POC. for a 6-week pilot we usually propose $X credits, but we'll tailor that based on expected token usage.
01:49 Luke Carter: can you be more specific on what those credits look like and any restrictions?
01:53 Maya Chen: sure. typical structure: a usage credit pool to cover the benchmark and a buffer for dev testing; credits apply only to Redwood-hosted endpoints unless you request dedicated reserved capacity, which would be quoted separately. any overage is billed at discounted pilot rates and we notify you before crossing thresholds.
02:09 Priya Singh: is there a minimum contract or commitment to move to Dedicated or Private after the POC?
02:14 Maya Chen: no mandatory commit; pilots are non-binding. If you want reserved capacity, we can discuss a term sheet, but it's not required to run the pilot.
02:21 Sarah Patel: and what about data residency and logs? we need audit logs and retention controls for PII.
02:27 Diego Ramos: audit logs are available; retention policies can be configured and we can also show an on-prem or VPC deployment for stricter retention. We'll include the options in the security packet.
02:36 Luke Carter: timeline wise, how long from dataset share to benchmark results?
02:40 Diego Ramos: typical turn around is 5 business days from receipt of cleaned sample and access details to run full benchmark, assuming no additional infra. if we need to provision dedicated nodes it could take extra 2-5 days.
02:53 Sarah Patel: okay that works. what about SLAs/canary rollouts? for production we'd want gradual rollout with fallback to baseline model.
02:59 Maya Chen: Redwood supports canary and A/B routing; we can set automatic fallback rules if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds. we'll include config examples in the runbook.
03:10 Priya Singh: procurement: who signs the pilot agreement? do we need a PO?
03:14 Maya Chen: pilots are covered by a simple SOW that references the pilot credits and scope; typically no large procurement required but if your finance team needs a PO we can accept that. For enterprise commitments we go through contracting.
03:25 Luke Carter: what about IP / data usage—do you retain any training rights?
03:29 Maya Chen: by default, customer data is not used to train Redwood public models; we can add explicit clauses to the SOW for data handling and retention to match your policy.
03:36 Sarah Patel: good. let's talk about metrics for passing the POC—are we agreeing to target thresholds?
03:40 Diego Ramos: suggested pass conditions: quality delta within 5% of baseline on ROUGE/med-entity metrics, p95 latency under 1.2s, and cost per 1k notes under $Y (to be filled once we estimate tokens). also uptime and stability over 2 week stress window.
03:56 Sarah Patel: that seems reasonable; we'll confirm the exact numbers when we see the first benchmark.
04:01 Maya Chen: for the commercial guardrails: we'll propose a pilot credit pool that covers the benchmark plus 2 weeks dev testing; notification thresholds at 50/75/90% usage and a hard cap that requires explicit approval to exceed.
04:16 Luke Carter: please include a cap and a point of contact for approval; finance won't want surprise bills.
04:20 Maya Chen: yes we'll include a designated billing contact and real-time usage dashboard access.
04:24 Priya Singh: and for the dedicated/private option: what are lead times and ballpark costs?
04:29 Diego Ramos: lead time for Private (VPC) is typically 2-4 weeks including network setup and certs; on-prem varies widely. cost depends on nodes and model class; we'll give an estimated price range in the SOW.
04:41 Sarah Patel: ok on next steps: Sarah to share anonymized dataset, Diego to share benchmark template, Maya to share pilot credit proposal and SOW draft, Priya to list compliance docs.
04:54 Maya Chen: we'll target sending the SOW and pilot terms by Friday 2025-02-15, is that okay?
04:58 Sarah Patel: yes that's fine.
05:02 Diego Ramos: can we lock in a benchmark kickoff for week of 2025-02-17?
05:06 Luke Carter: that works on our side, pending dataset share on Friday.
05:10 Priya Singh: I'll gather security asks by 2025-02-14.
05:14 Maya Chen: perfect. any other questions or blockers?
05:17 Sarah Patel: just one: can the pilot include a small user study with clinicians to capture acceptance rate?
05:22 Diego Ramos: absolutely — we can instrument review flows and capture accept/modify/reject stats and show annotation UI snapshots.
05:29 Sarah Patel: awesome.
05:31 Maya Chen: great. quick recap of next steps (we'll also email): 1) Sarah share sample dataset + baseline metrics, 2) Diego sends benchmarking runbook and template, 3) Maya shares SOW/pilot credit proposal, 4) Priya shares compliance doc list. schedule benchmark for week of 2025-02-17.
05:54 Luke Carter: thanks everyone, look forward to the SOW.
05:57 Maya Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the kickoff. bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker tag switch and minor word errors (e.g., KMS spelled kms, ROUGE might be transcribed as rouge). references to dollar values and exact credit numbers left blank to be tailored once token estimates are calculated.

References / links mentioned: Pilot SOW template (link sent via email), Benchmark runbook (will be shared by Diego), Security pack (SOC2, encryption, KMS integration)
